questions.text: Members of Kingdom Monera are fundamentally characterised by which type of cellular organisation?
Which of the following is characteristic of a typical prokaryotic cell?
options: Genetic material not enclosed within a membrane-bound nucleus

questions.text: Which cellular structure is present in typical bacteria and is responsible for protein synthesis?
The ribosomes of typical bacterial cells are:
Which statement about the organisation of monerans is correct?
options: All monerans possess a true nucleus.
Monerans are unicellular prokaryotes, although they may form colonies or filaments.

questions.text: Which of the following structures is absent in a typical bacterial cell?
Which statement about the cell wall of bacteria is correct?
options: Every organism placed in Monera has a cell wall.
Typical bacteria possess a cell wall, but Mycoplasma lacks one.
Bacterial cell walls are made of cellulose.
Bacteria lack both cell walls and plasma membranes.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about bacterial nutrition is correct?
options: Bacteria may be autotrophic or heterotrophic.
Bacteria cannot obtain energy from inorganic substances.

questions.text: Which of the following can occur among members of Kingdom Monera?
Which process is commonly associated with bacterial reproduction?
options: Meiosis followed by fertilisation in every species
Spore formation as the only method

questions.text: Which statement about the habitat of monerans is correct?
options: They occupy diverse habitats, including ordinary and extreme environments.
They occur exclusively inside host organisms.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a general characteristic of typical bacteria?
Bacteria may form filaments or colonies. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Every colony of bacteria is a multicellular eukaryote.
Colonial or filamentous growth does not make bacteria eukaryotic.
Filamentous bacteria necessarily possess membrane-bound nuclei.
All bacterial colonies are reproductive structures.

questions.text: Which feature most fundamentally distinguishes Monera from the other four kingdoms in Whittaker's five-kingdom classification?
Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Bacteria may have diverse nutritional modes.
All monerans possess a cell wall.

questions.text: Archaebacteria are particularly distinguished from other bacteria in the traditional NCERT account by differences in their:
Which of the following is NOT one of the three major groups of archaebacteria described in NCERT?
Halophiles are adapted to environments characterised by:
Which habitat is most characteristic of halophiles?
Thermoacidophiles are associated with environments that are:
Which environment is a suitable example of the habitat of thermoacidophiles?
options: A neutral freshwater pond at ordinary temperature

questions.text: Methanogens are particularly associated with:
options: Anaerobic environments, including the rumen of ruminants

questions.text: Which gas is characteristically produced by methanogens?
Methanogens found in the rumen of cattle are significant because they:
options: Convert methane into oxygen as their defining process.
Contribute to methane production under anaerobic conditions.
Cause all digestion in cattle by producing digestive enzymes.

questions.text: Which pair is correctly matched?
options: Halophiles — methane production as their defining characteristic

questions.text: Which pair is incorrectly matched?
Which group of archaebacteria is most likely to be found in a highly saline lake?
Which group is most closely associated with methane production in anaerobic digestive environments?
A microorganism is isolated from a hot, acidic spring. Which group would be the most appropriate initial identification based on its habitat?
Which statement about archaebacteria is correct?
options: All archaebacteria are oxygenic photosynthetic organisms.
All archaebacteria inhabit only ordinary environments.
Different groups are adapted to distinct environmental conditions.

questions.text: Which characteristic is an important distinguishing feature of archaebacteria in NCERT's account?
Which statement about methanogens is incorrect?
options: They can occur in anaerobic environments.
They are associated with the rumen of ruminants.
Their defining metabolic role is oxygenic photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which of the following sequences correctly matches each group with its characteristic association?
Which statement should be avoided when describing archaebacteria?
options: Different archaebacterial groups show different environmental adaptations.
Their cell-wall composition is an important distinguishing feature.
Every archaebacterium necessarily inhabits an extreme environment.

questions.text: Which of the following is the most accurate distinction between methanogens and thermoacidophiles?
options: Methanogens are defined by methane production, whereas thermoacidophiles are associated with hot, acidic conditions.
Methanogens are eukaryotes, whereas thermoacidophiles are prokaryotes.
Methanogens are plants, whereas thermoacidophiles are fungi.
Methanogens perform oxygenic photosynthesis, whereas thermoacidophiles never carry out metabolism.

questions.text: Eubacteria are commonly referred to as:
Which feature is characteristic of typical eubacteria?
Which of the following bacterial shapes is correctly matched?
Spherical-shaped bacteria are called:
Rod-shaped bacteria are called:
Which of the following is the correct general association?
options: Cocci — spherical; bacilli — rod-shaped; spirilla — spiral-shaped
Cocci — rod-shaped; bacilli — spherical; spirilla — spiral-shaped
Cocci — spiral-shaped; bacilli — rod-shaped; spirilla — spherical
Cocci — spherical; bacilli — spiral-shaped; spirilla — rod-shaped

questions.text: Which structure is primarily associated with bacterial motility in many bacteria?
Which statement about bacterial cell walls is correct?
options: All bacteria have cellulose cell walls.
Typical bacterial cell walls differ in composition from plant cell walls.
The cell wall is a membrane-bound organelle.

questions.text: Which structure contains the principal chromosomal genetic material in a typical prokaryotic cell?
options: Nucleus surrounded by a nuclear envelope

questions.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a typical bacterial cell from a typical eukaryotic cell?
Cyanobacteria are traditionally referred to as:
Cyanobacteria are classified as prokaryotes because they:
Which pigment is particularly important in the oxygenic photosynthesis of cyanobacteria?
Which process is characteristic of photosynthetic cyanobacteria?
options: Methane production as the defining process of every species

questions.text: Which of the following is a cyanobacterium?
Which of the following genera is associated with cyanobacteria?
Which statement about cyanobacteria is correct?
options: All cyanobacteria are unicellular and never form colonies.
Cyanobacteria may occur as unicellular, colonial or filamentous forms.

questions.text: Cyanobacteria are found in which of the following environments?
Which structure is associated with nitrogen fixation in certain cyanobacteria?
Which of the following cyanobacteria is associated with heterocyst formation?
Which statement about heterocysts is correct?
options: They are found in every bacterial species.
They are specialised cells associated with nitrogen fixation in certain cyanobacteria.
They are the reproductive spores of fungi.

questions.text: Which of the following is a common NCERT example of a cyanobacterium associated with nitrogen fixation?
Which statement correctly distinguishes photosynthesis from nitrogen fixation?
options: Both terms mean the production of methane.
Nitrogen fixation is simply another name for photosynthesis.
Every photosynthetic organism necessarily fixes atmospheric nitrogen.
Photosynthesis produces organic compounds using light energy, whereas nitrogen fixation converts atmospheric nitrogen into biologically usable forms.

questions.text: Which statement is incorrect?
options: Certain cyanobacteria can fix atmospheric nitrogen.

questions.text: A filamentous prokaryote contains chlorophyll a and specialised cells associated with nitrogen fixation. Which identification is most appropriate?
Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria obtain energy primarily by:
options: Breaking down food inside a digestive tract

questions.text: Which of the following may serve as an inorganic substrate for chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria?
Chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria use the energy obtained from inorganic substances to:
Which ecological process is supported by chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria?
options: Conversion of all organic matter into oxygen

questions.text: Which of the following nutrients is associated with the cycling activities of chemosynthetic bacteria described in NCERT?
Which statement about chemosynthetic autotrophs is correct?
options: They obtain all their energy directly from sunlight.
They can obtain energy by oxidising inorganic substances.

questions.text: A bacterium oxidises inorganic compounds and uses the released energy to synthesise organic material. It is best described as:
Which statement correctly distinguishes chemosynthetic autotrophy from photosynthetic autotrophy?
options: Chemosynthetic autotrophy is exclusively an animal process.
Chemosynthetic autotrophy obtains energy through chemical oxidation, whereas photosynthetic autotrophy uses light energy.
Photosynthetic autotrophy does not require an energy source.

questions.text: Which statement about the ecological significance of chemosynthetic autotrophic bacteria is incorrect?
options: They use chemical energy to synthesise organic compounds.
They are ecologically insignificant because they cannot contribute to nutrient cycles.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations is correct?
options: Chemosynthetic autotrophs — ingestion of food — digestive tract
Chemosynthetic autotrophs — oxidation of inorganic substances — nutrient recycling
Chemosynthetic autotrophs — exclusively methane production in the rumen

questions.text: Heterotrophic bacteria obtain organic nutrients from:
options: Carbon dioxide alone in every case
Inorganic substances alone in every case
Sunlight without any material source of nutrients

questions.text: Which role is commonly performed by heterotrophic bacteria in ecosystems?
options: Conversion of every organism into a virus
Prevention of all organic matter breakdown

questions.text: Heterotrophic bacteria are important in food production and other useful processes. Which statement is correct?
options: Heterotrophic bacteria cannot be used in food production.
Heterotrophic bacteria never participate in decomposition.
Some heterotrophic bacteria are useful in food production and other processes.

questions.text: Which statement about disease-causing bacteria is correct?
options: Some bacteria are pathogenic, but many are harmless or beneficial.

questions.text: A bacterium breaks down dead organic matter and helps return nutrients to the environment. Its ecological role is best described as:
options: Producer through oxygenic photosynthesis in every case

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Some heterotrophic bacteria are useful to humans.

questions.text: Which statement best describes the ecological significance of bacterial decomposers?
options: They contribute to the breakdown of organic matter and nutrient recycling.
They prevent dead organisms from decomposing.
They eliminate nitrogen from every ecosystem.
They convert all inorganic material directly into animals.

questions.text: Which statement about bacterial nutrition is most accurate?
options: Heterotrophic bacteria cannot survive in organic-rich environments.
Bacteria exhibit diverse nutritional strategies, including autotrophy and heterotrophy.

questions.text: A bacterium causes a disease in a host. Which term best describes the bacterium's disease-causing capacity?
Which conclusion is justified by the diversity of heterotrophic bacteria?
options: Every heterotroph must be a parasite.
Heterotrophic bacteria can have ecological, industrial, beneficial and harmful roles.
Heterotrophic bacteria cannot decompose organic matter.

questions.text: The common mode of asexual reproduction in bacteria is:
During binary fission, a bacterial cell generally:
options: Undergoes meiosis to produce four haploid cells.

questions.text: Which statement about bacterial reproduction is correct?
options: All bacteria reproduce exclusively by fungal-type spore formation.
Binary fission is a common method of bacterial reproduction.
Bacteria must undergo sexual reproduction to multiply.

questions.text: Under favourable conditions, many bacteria can multiply rapidly by:
Bacterial spore formation, as discussed in NCERT, is particularly associated with:
options: Survival under unfavourable conditions in certain bacteria

questions.text: Which statement about bacterial spores is correct?
options: Every bacterial spore is a fungal reproductive spore.
Bacterial spores are always fragile and immediately destroyed by environmental stress.
Some bacterial spores are highly resistant and aid survival under unfavourable conditions.

questions.text: Which statement correctly distinguishes survival-oriented bacterial spore formation from ordinary binary fission?
options: Binary fission always forms resistant spores.
Binary fission is a common reproductive method, whereas certain bacterial spores aid survival under adverse conditions.
Spore formation always produces four daughter cells through meiosis.

questions.text: Which of the following is a mechanism of genetic recombination in bacteria?
options: Fertilisation between male and female flowers

questions.text: Which of the following lists the three commonly described bacterial genetic recombination mechanisms?
The direct transfer of genetic material from one bacterial cell to another through cell-to-cell contact is called:
The uptake of free DNA from the environment by a bacterial cell is called:
The transfer of bacterial DNA mediated by a bacteriophage is called:
Which mechanism is correctly matched with its defining process?
options: Conjugation — transfer mediated by a bacteriophage
Transduction — direct cell-to-cell transfer as its defining feature
Binary fission — uptake of environmental DNA

questions.text: Which mechanism of bacterial genetic recombination involves a bacteriophage?
A bacterial cell acquires DNA released into its environment by another cell. Which mechanism is illustrated?
A bacterial virus transfers genetic material from one bacterium to another. Which process is involved?
Which statement about bacterial genetic recombination is correct?
options: Conjugation, transformation and transduction are recognised mechanisms of genetic recombination.
All three mechanisms are forms of mitosis.
All three require flowers and seeds.
All three are identical to binary fission.

questions.text: Which statement about binary fission and genetic recombination is most accurate?
options: Binary fission and transformation are identical processes.
Conjugation always produces four daughter cells.
Transduction is another name for binary fission.
Binary fission is a reproductive process, whereas transformation is a mechanism of genetic recombination.

questions.text: Which option correctly matches all three genetic recombination mechanisms?
options: Conjugation—free DNA uptake; transformation—bacteriophage; transduction—cell contact
Conjugation—direct cell-to-cell transfer; transformation—free DNA uptake; transduction—bacteriophage-mediated transfer

questions.text: Which statement about bacterial reproduction and recombination is incorrect?
options: Binary fission is common in bacteria.
Certain bacteria form resistant spores under unfavourable conditions.
Bacteria can exchange or acquire genetic material through different mechanisms.
Conjugation, transformation and transduction are all identical forms of binary fission.

questions.text: Which characteristic distinguishes Mycoplasma from typical bacteria?
Mycoplasma is particularly notable because its members are:
options: Among the smallest living cellular organisms
Organisms that lack all metabolic activity

questions.text: Which statement about Mycoplasma is correct?
options: It always possesses a rigid cell wall.

questions.text: Which characteristic contributes to the variable shape, or pleomorphism, of Mycoplasma?
options: Presence of a rigid cellulose wall

questions.text: Which statement about the oxygen requirements of Mycoplasma is consistent with NCERT?
options: Some species can survive without oxygen.

questions.text: Which statement about the pathogenicity of Mycoplasma is correct?
options: All species are harmless to every organism.
All species are photosynthetic pathogens of plants.
Mycoplasma cannot be associated with disease.

questions.text: Which combination best describes Mycoplasma?
options: Prokaryotic, without a cell wall and pleomorphic
Eukaryotic, without genetic material and without ribosomes
Prokaryotic, with chloroplasts and a rigid cellulose wall

questions.text: Which statement about the cell wall of Mycoplasma is correct?
options: It is always identical to the cell wall of plants.

questions.text: An organism is cellular, prokaryotic, lacks a cell wall and displays variable shapes. Which identification best fits these characteristics?
Which statement is incorrect about Mycoplasma?
options: It is a eukaryotic organism with membrane-bound mitochondria.
It is among the smallest living cellular organisms.

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about Kingdom Monera.

1. Monerans are prokaryotic.
2. Typical bacterial cells contain 70S ribosomes.
3. All monerans possess a cell wall.
Choose the correct answer.

Consider the following statements about archaebacteria.

1. Halophiles are associated with highly saline environments.
2. Thermoacidophiles are associated with hot, acidic environments.
3. Methanogens produce methane and may occur in anaerobic environments.
Choose the correct answer.

Consider the following statements about cyanobacteria.

1. Cyanobacteria are prokaryotic.
2. Certain cyanobacteria possess heterocysts associated with nitrogen fixation.
3. All cyanobacteria possess heterocysts.
Choose the correct answer.

Consider the following statements about bacterial genetic recombination.

1. Conjugation involves direct cell-to-cell transfer.
2. Transformation involves the uptake of free DNA.
3. Transduction involves bacteriophage-mediated DNA transfer.
Choose the correct answer.

### Assertion–reason questions
For Questions 115–118, use these options:

A. Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
B. Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion.
C. Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
D. Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

Assertion: Cyanobacteria are classified as prokaryotes.

Reason: Cyanobacteria lack a membrane-bound nucleus.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.text:
Assertion: All bacteria are harmful to humans.

Reason: Some bacteria are useful in food production, decomposition and other processes.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.text:
Assertion: Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall.

Reason: The absence of a cell wall is associated with its variable shape.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.text:
Assertion: Transformation and transduction are identical mechanisms of bacterial genetic recombination.

Reason: Transformation involves the uptake of free DNA, whereas transduction involves bacteriophage-mediated DNA transfer.

### Advanced application questions
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not correctly explain Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.

questions.text:
Three microorganisms are isolated:

- Organism X thrives in highly saline conditions.
- Organism Y produces methane under anaerobic conditions.
- Organism Z is a photosynthetic prokaryote with heterocysts.
Which identification is correct?

Consider the following observations about an unidentified microorganism:

- It is cellular and prokaryotic.
- It lacks a cell wall.
- It has no membrane-bound nucleus.
- It may display variable shapes.
Which conclusion is most appropriate?
options: It must be a photosynthetic cyanobacterium.
It must be a typical wall-bearing eubacterium.
It must be a unicellular eukaryotic fungus.
